seo.title: What Is Hakomi? | Tender of the Soul
seo.description: Learn about Hakomi, a mindful, body-centered approach to present-moment experience.

hero.title: Listen beneath the words.
hero.introduction: Hakomi is a gentle, mindful, body-centered approach that follows present-moment experience with curiosity and compassion.

overview.lead: The body can reveal information that is not yet available to the conscious mind.
overview.paragraphOne: Rather than relying entirely on analysis or conversation, Hakomi invites us to notice the small, often overlooked ways experience is happening now: a held breath, a change in posture, an emotion at the edge of awareness, an impulse to move closer or pull away.
overview.paragraphTwo: These are not problems to correct. They are doorways into the beliefs and organizing patterns that may be shaping how you relate, protect yourself, and imagine what is possible.

foundations.heading: A slower, kinder kind of attention.

items.title: Mindfulness
items.description: Slowing down enough to notice what is happening, here and now.

items.title: The body
items.description: Listening for information held in sensation, breath, posture, and movement.

items.title: Curiosity
items.description: Meeting experience gently, without diagnosing, forcing, or rushing to fix it.

items.title: Transformation
items.description: Making space for old beliefs and patterns to become visible and begin to change.

process.heading: From unconscious pattern to possibility.
process.paragraphOne: Core beliefs can quietly organize our experience. They influence what we expect, what we notice, and which futures feel available to us.
process.paragraphTwo: Through mindful contact with present-moment experience, these patterns may become visible. When they are safely felt and met, their charge can begin to soften, creating space for different choices, relationships, and ways of being.
process.statement: When your inner architecture shifts, new possibilities become available.

related.heading: Related ways of working
related.paragraphOne: Elana’s work is trauma informed and may draw from or share principles with mindfulness, somatic approaches, attachment-oriented work, Internal Family Systems-informed perspectives, and Somatic Experiencing-informed principles, Jungian thought and dream analysis, and Non Violent Communication.
related.paragraphTwo: This language describes influences and shared principles only; it does not claim formal certification in these modalities. Verified training details will be added to the About page before publication.

fit.heading: Is Hakomi right for me?
fit.body: You do not need to be comfortable with your body, good at mindfulness, or able to name exactly what you feel. Curiosity is enough. If you want a process that includes more than talking and respects your pace, Hakomi may offer a meaningful place to begin.
